cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For AX-17 in Germany, the renal dose modification guidance is as follows [E2]:
*   **Normal renal category** (eGFR >=90): Starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2].
*   **Mild renal category** (eGFR 60-89): Starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, and monitoring is routine [E2].
*   **Moderate renal category** (eGFR 30-59): Starting dose is 25 mg OD, maximum is 50 mg/day, and monitoring requires recheck 2-4 weeks [E2]. The approved German renal starting dose for moderate renal impairment is 25 mg once daily [E1, E3].
*   **Severe renal category** (eGFR 15-29): Requires specialist review, maximum is 25 mg/day, and monitoring is enhanced [E2].

*   Normal renal category: 50 mg OD [E2]
*   Mild renal category: 50 mg OD [E2]

Specifically, the historical fact for moderate renal impairment starting dose was 50 mg once daily [E3].

cases.question: What does SB-AX17-2026-09 require?
cases.answer:
The HelixNova Safety Bulletin SB-AX17-2026-09 requires baseline hepatic laboratory values with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1]. Additionally, specific actions are required based on hepatic laboratory results: a medical review if ALT/AST is >3x ULN, an urgent review if Bilirubin is >2x ULN, and a repeat test if there is a mild isolated change below trigger [E2].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 12.7%, Headache 14.0%, Fatigue 15.3%, Dizziness 16.6%, Rash 17.8%, and Transaminase elevation 19.1% [E1]. For the control group in HN-204, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E1]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-204, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E1].

In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 11.8%, Headache 13.0%, Fatigue 14.2%, Dizziness 15.4%, Rash 16.6%, and Transaminase elevation 17.7% [E2]. For the control group in HN-311, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E2]. Transaminase elevation was reported as serious in HN-311, while Nausea, Headache, Fatigue, Dizziness, and Rash were not serious [E2].

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the AX-17 % for all listed adverse events was lower in HN-311. Specifically, the AX-17 % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) were: Nausea -0.9 points, Headache -1.0 points, Fatigue -1.1 points, Dizziness -1.2 points, Rash -1.2 points, and Transaminase elevation -1.4 points [E4]. All AX-17 % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4]. The control % for all listed adverse events was the same in both studies, with a difference of +0.0 points for each event when comparing HN-311 to HN-204 [E4].

In both studies, the highest AX-17 % was for Transaminase elevation: 19.1% in HN-204 and 17.7% in HN-311 [E4].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

Descriptive comparison across separate studies, not a head-to-head result.
